utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is case number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic, Dragan Obrenovic, and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, before we have the first witness today, is there anything that both parties would like to bring to the attention to this Tribunal? Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Before the next witness testifies, I would like -- I'm requesting a curative -- a cautionary instruction to the Prosecution and to the witness that the Prosecutor not ask for conclusions and that the witness not volunteer conclusions based on the summary -- the summaries that he will be given. I brought this matter to the attention of the Prosecution during the 65 ter meeting, mentioning the Milosevic decision. It's an Appeals Chamber decision dated 30th September 2002. During the 65 ter meeting, I believe, and I trust that the Prosecution misspoke when it said that this Trial Chamber is not bound by other decisions. That may be the case with respect to Trial Chamber decisions; however, in the Aleksovski judgement, the appeal judgement, it's very clear, it's been made clear also in this particular case and two appeals, interlocutory appeals, that a Trial Chamber is bound by the decisions from the Appeals Chamber. I'm sure Your Honours know that. So I trust that Mr. McCloskey misspoke at the time. But nonetheless, I think it would be prudent perhaps to caution both the Prosecution and the witness that they're not to provide any conclusions but merely a summary of -- and to comply strictly with the decision of the Milosevic decision, which I'm sure the Prosecution is fully cognisant of. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for bringing to our attention this issue, but we believe that it's a little bit premature to raise it. But as a precautionary measure, we'll take it and we'll tell both parties that the witness should testify as to what he saw and what he heard, not draw any conclusions and opinions. Yes. Shall we start?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'm terribly sorry. I do have one matter to bring up before the Trial Chamber, and I think that the record we make in a 65 ter meeting is as valid as a record in open court, I'm assuming? Is it public record? Because I want to openly object before we proceed to trial that the Defence counsels do not abide by or accept or acquiesce to the acceptance of the payment proposal by the Registrar. And as an example of how seriously this affects the rights of the accused, I would like to submit what is going to be marked D1/3, and it's a copy of an ethics complaint against the Registry which affects my licence in the state of Texas, and I would like for the Court to be aware of this, knowing that we are going to trial because we have an obligation to our client but by going to trial I want to assure the Trial Chamber that we are not acquiescing and accepting the payment proposal of the Registrar at the moment. We believe it violates the rights of the accused. So may I offer these to the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. Of course we'll bring this matter to the attention of the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'd also like to address the next witness that we have. Basically, I know that this is untimely, and I ask the Court's leave to challenge the competency of this expert witness, which should have been done, I believe, 20 days after we got notice of his being offered as an expert witness. But we never have received a statement of this witness. Therefore, I don't believe that he can fit into the category of an expert. And because we've never received a CV, we don't know his training from the past, it can't be stipulated that he has expertise in any area. I'd like this witness to be treated as a regular witness and not an expert witness and be prevented from coming to conclusions or opinions on any of the witnesses he's interviewed. And under the Milosevic decision, that he not be allowed to summarise any witness statements unless he provides us with a list of the witnesses that he's relying upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I have to say that the situation in this case is different from Milosevic's case. I don't think that witness will summarise any statement of the witnesses. Secondly, at the very beginning of the trial I think the Prosecutor will ask some questions, try to qualify this witness, like his background, his experience, whether he has firsthand knowledge of what happened, et cetera. Thirdly, could I ask the Prosecutor to explain to me whether they have treated the first witness as an expert witness or just an ordinary witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Your Honour, Stacy de la Torre for the Prosecution. Mr. Ruez is a fact witness in this case. He personally visited the crime scenes and will be a foundational witness for all of the evidence presented regarding the crime scenes. However, he can offer his conclusions as to what was found at each of those crime scenes based upon his investigation and his expertise as the lead investigator on this investigation and as a law enforcement official.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope that you could bear in mind there are some objections from the Defence team on this very issue and very carefully conduct your direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I have one more --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is there anything else? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I would like to ask the Court to rule on a motion in limine, pre-trial, before -- I mean, pre-testimony before Mr. Ruez testifies not to allude to terms such as "massacres", "ethnically cleansed" or holocaust as he did in his prior testimony. Those are prejudicial terms and not terms that a fact witness should be using in his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid, you know, that request is too high. I think the witness could use whatever language he could, but it depends on the Trial Chamber whether to take it or not. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. De la Torre, taking your special conditions, this Chamber will permit you to take a seat if necessary while presenting your evidence. If you need to have a short break, just let us know.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have the first witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please take the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper that the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Ms. De la Torre.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, could you please state your name for the record?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: My name is Jean-Rene Ruez, R-u-e-z.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And is it correct to say, Mr. Ruez that, you were formerly employed as an investigator here at the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. I have worked as the Office of the Prosecutor from 1995 through 2001.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly request that the speakers pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question. We have to give some delay to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Prior to coming to the Tribunal, could you explain to the Court where you worked.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I am chief superintendent currently in the Ministry of Interior, judicial police branch of the French police.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And you indicated that you came to the Tribunal in 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Do you recall when it was that you arrived at the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: My first day working in the Tribunal was 7 April 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: When were you assigned to the Srebrenica investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In July 1995, when the first press rumours reached the Tribunal, a decision was made to check that information and I was sent down to Tuzla, where I arrived -- I think it was 20 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Were you the first investigator assigned to the Srebrenica investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: When you arrived on the scene in Tuzla July 20th, 1995, did you initiate an investigation that you headed until you left the Tribunal in 2001?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. As soon as we started with the investigation in Tuzla, it appeared that the scale of the events was huge, and that investigation never stopped, not only when I left -- when I left, it continued. So it's still ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: From July 1995 until your departure in 2001, did you focus almost exclusively on the Srebrenica investigation and the events surrounding the fall of the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, exclusively. It was my only assignment after that summer 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, before we get into what you discovered during the course of your investigation, I'd like to talk about the exhibits that will be introduced during the course of your testimony. You testified in a previous case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to review the exhibits that were introduced during the course of your testimony in the Krstic case in preparation for this trial?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And did you assist the Prosecution in selecting the exhibits that you felt were most important with regard to the presentation of your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: In the interest of expediency and clarity, did you assist the Prosecution in marking those exhibits with the relevant points of interest?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: The exhibits that are going to be introduced today and in the next few days during the course of your testimony, the markings that are on them, were those markings made with your guidance and at your direction?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. I -- I indicated what the markings should be on these pictures.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, could you give the Court an orientation using the map here before you of Srebrenica and where it is geographically, vis-a-vis Serbia and the BiH territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. De la Torre, I'm sorry to interrupt. Before you come to the specific issues, could you ask a question about the present occupation of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, a question about ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: About the present occupation of this witness. We haven't heard it yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Sure, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. Presently I am on a leave of absence from my administration. I requested that leave when I left this Tribunal in April 2001. That means, in other terms, that I am on holidays since April 2001. I'm restarting professional activities in July this year.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: When you return to your employment in July of 2003, where will you be assigned?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I've requested to be assigned at the international cooperation service that we have at the Ministry of Interior in France.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And what will your duties be in that capacity?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I will be heading a department in charge of raising funds for international cooperation projects.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: If you could, Mr. Ruez, using the map before you, could you just orient the Court to Srebrenica and where it lies vis-a-vis the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So on this map, the enclave is located at the bottom right of the exhibit, and the grey outline is -- marks the limits of the safe area of Srebrenica. And I say on purpose "the limits," and not "the border," since borders have never been established. Approximately 4 kilometres east is the Drina River, the Drina River being the border with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. And approximately 20 kilometres west of the enclave, the grey outline at the left of the exhibit marks the confrontation line that at that time was separating Muslim-held territory, on the left of the map, from the Serb-held territory, as the east, so at the right of the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, approximately how far is it from Srebrenica towards Tuzla, which would be considered in Bosnian free territory at the time?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Walking distance in a straight line would be approximately 60 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. And for the record, you were referring to Prosecution Exhibit 24. Mr. Ruez, we'll move now to Prosecution Exhibit 1.1. And if you could, please, explain to the Court what it is that they're seeing in this video.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Full screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So this video is a helicopter view, filmed from the south of the Srebrenica enclave, flying towards Srebrenica. The aim of this video is to give the Chamber an indication of how the terrain looks like in this area. It's very big hills with deep valleys. It's a kind of a pre-mountainous terrain. And in fact, the south of the enclave is the most difficult terrain in this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Did you yourself take this footage?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did. This is a view of Srebrenica town. There's a last hill, and then one enters the valley, and at the bottom of this valley is Srebrenica town. The quality is not so -- so good. So it's a town that's stretched inside this valley in between two steep hills. On this view is the centre town, where the former main mosque was and at the time this film was shot the mosque had been transformed into a parking lot.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: When was this video taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In 1998. The destruction of the mosque of the Srebrenica town was a slow process, but it started instantly during the summer 1995. This is the location of Company B of the UN Battalion that was located inside the enclave, and this is the direction that then will lead towards Potocari, where is located -- it's a pity that the picture disappeared -- just behind the hill that was at the end of that landscape.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, for the Prosecutor, please. And could the speakers slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: You indicated in the video there was a Company B, which was the headquarters of the UN Battalion. Did the UN Battalion stationed in the Srebrenica area have more than one compound?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The main headquarters were located in a factory in Potocari, approximately 4 or 5 kilometres away from Srebrenica town. And inside Srebrenica town was a smaller detachment, named Company B.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 1.3, are you able, using this map, to see not only Srebrenica but also towards the direction of Potocari where the main UN compound was located?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No. This photograph shows the view that one has on Srebrenica town when coming from the south, so this is the view that the Bosnian Serb soldiers, who were the first ones to enter Srebrenica town, could see. This is the last hill before entering Srebrenica town.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you would prefer, I believe we're done with this map for the time being. And if I would have it taken down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll have it moved.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: You indicated, Mr. Ruez, that this was the view from the south. When the Srebrenica enclave fell in July 1995, what direction -- from which direction did the Serbs advance?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: They were advancing from the south towards the north, so in the direction that -- that the helicopter took when I showed the previous exhibit. This is the direction that the Bosnian Serb army took when they entered the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: When did Srebrenica fall?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The fall of the enclave is dated 11 July 1995, once the population realises that an airstrike that just occurred would not be sufficient --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object at this point. He's giving a conclusion. The witness is giving a conclusion at this point and we don't have the predicate foundation. He's beginning to testify about events which he did not witness. If a foundation wants to be laid as far as who he spoke with and how he has this knowledge, then perhaps I won't be objecting. But so far I haven't heard a basis upon which he can formulate these conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the Prosecutor is just asking this question, and later on she will lead us to that point. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I can, however, ask Mr. Ruez a few foundational questions with regard to the extent of his investigation in his six years as the lead investigator on this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And Mr. Karnavas, I have to remind you that the hearsay evidence is acceptable, admissible, in this Tribunal, which is different from other jurisdictions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do understand that hearsay is admissible. However, I have no basis of knowing how this gentleman has reached these conclusions, because the foundation wasn't laid. And I do take your point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, beginning in July 1995, when you arrived in Tuzla, did you begin speaking to witnesses who had fled and survived the fall of the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. At that time the situation was that me and a few assistants who were confronted to that situation were facing 25.000 refugees who were in the Tuzla area, so the initial process was in fact to scan the work that had been started by local police and the local war crime commission in order to identify the most useful witnesses, in order to begin to have a clear picture of what had happened during -- during these days. So for instance, when I say that the enclave fell 11 July 1995, because at that moment the population realised that the airstrike that occurred would not be enough a measure to stop the advance of the Drina Corps, this information is based on the interviews that we conducted with I would say in total approximately 100 people, who more or less all of them used that event, the airstrike event, to mark the moment where they personally considered that the enclave was lost and that the only solution that was left to them was to flee. So this is the reason why I date the fall of the enclave 11 July.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And during the course of your six years investigating this particular case, Mr. Ruez, how many people would you estimate that you personally interviewed with regard to these events?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It would be difficult for me to answer that question, since we interviewed various categories of witnesses, those -- those we call the victims. Others are members of the International Community. Others are former UN soldiers. I don't know, maybe I interviewed personally some 50 victims of the events of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And during the course of your investigation, did you supervise other investigators who continued the process of interviewing witnesses with regard to the events leading up to and following the fall of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, sure. As soon as a structured team was put in function, I was following the activities of -- following and directing the activities of all the team members and following up with all the information that they could collect related to the subject.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And has the -- is the fact that the enclave fell on the 11th of July, has that ever been seriously in dispute with regard to the witness testimony?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I don't think so, since even General Krstic, I think, would -- would say that the fall of the enclave is dated 11 of July, since this is the day when the first elements of the Drina Corps entered the town and this is the day where Mladic also entered the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Have you personally seen videotape dated 11 July of -- and 12 July as well of General Mladic marching through Srebrenica after its fall?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. And we will present these footages that have been presented on television in Republika Srpska at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Based upon your interviews with witnesses who survived the fall of the enclave, were you able to determine how the population reacted once it became clear that Srebrenica was going to fall?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, they reacted both by instinct and also by order. Some people took the decision on their own to flee either -- there were two directions of flight. Part of the population, mostly the women and the elderly, fled towards Potocari, and this for two reasons: One was by instinct, to try to find shelter in the vicinity of UN soldiers; but also because the rumour anyhow was spread among the population that this was the course of action that they were supposed to take. For the men, it was another course of action, and also following instructions that were repeated by the people among them, that the men should assemble in an area at the north of the enclave, that is, the area of the villages of Susnjari and Zagarici and this in order then to attempt a break-through out of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: We'll take those two issues separately, Mr. Ruez. So starting just with Potocari and the refugees who made the decision to go to Potocari, based upon your investigation, how many people are estimated to have chosen to flee to Potocari rather than trek through the woods?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So as soon as we talk about large numbers, it's always difficult to be precise. The general assessment is that approximately 25.000 people fled towards Potocari, and this is the number of people who ultimately, roughly the number of people who ultimately arrived in Tuzla following the deportation process, so approximately 25.000. That group was composed, as I said, essentially of women, children, and elderly, but also of an unknown number of men who didn't want to abandon their families in that circumstance and also men who thought that it was safe enough to stay there and become a prisoner of the Serb forces and later be exchanged. They accepted to take that option.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And just for the sake of clarity, Mr. Ruez, what was in Potocari that these people were fleeing toward?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: They were fleeing towards Potocari because Potocari was the location where the main US base was located, so the aim of all these people was to be as close as possible to these UN soldiers in order to be protected.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: We'll turn now, Mr. Ruez, to Prosecution Exhibit 2.1, which is a videotape of Potocari. If you could, please, indicate to the Judges what it is that they'll be seeing on this particular video.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Before the video, there was another exhibit that was just on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 1.3, an aerial view of the entire valley.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: There is -- go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So the aim of this exhibit is to -- to show the distance, in fact, between Srebrenica town and Potocari. So this is a still photograph extracted from the videotape that was presented as the first exhibit. At the bottom of the yellow line marks the road that goes down towards Srebrenica town. Then one can see the town itself, that is very thin and long in this valley. And at a distance of approximately 4 kilometres, where it is written "Potocari," just behind the -- that hill is the location of Potocari. And at the distance is the town of Bratunac, in the mist, at the top right of the photograph. And the arrow at the top of the picture, pointing towards Konjevic Polje indicates the asphalt road that goes from Bratunac towards Konjevic Polje, and that is located behind that hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And just for scale, Mr. Ruez, how far is it roughly from Potocari to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Then from Potocari to Bratunac it's again a short distance of approximately 3 to 4 kilometres, 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning now to Prosecution Exhibit 2.1, the video of Potocari, did you take this video, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That first part shows again Srebrenica town. I am -- I shot that video in 1998. The beginning is the same than what we saw previously, but then the film is going to switch towards Potocari. And once in Potocari, I'm not the one who filmed the pictures. They were filmed by another member of the Office of the Prosecutor with whom I went on mission in April 1996 and who filmed the pictures that we will see later on the ground in Potocari. So this is going towards Potocari -- towards Potocari, behind this big hill at the left of the picture is going to be the location Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Were you present when this video footage was taken of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This one, I filmed this part, and the part that will follow I was indeed present. So this is Potocari. Potocari is a small industrial area composed of a group of six factories, in fact, seven, I think. Here we can see some of these that we will show later on stills. This is a bus compound, it's a bus company. This is a zinc factory. And then here, here, this main -- this one is -- that's another location, which is called the White House. Just in front is another factory. And here, this main, this main factory is the main UN base in Potocari. It's located in a former battery factory, and it's called the Akumulator factory. So this is filmed from the road. This is coming from Srebrenica towards Potocari, so this is the direction that the refugees took. Here comes one first factory where the people assembled. This one is the Energoinvest 11 of March factory. Then comes the zinc factory, the so-called zinc factory, which is also an Energoinvest building. This building is simply called by everyone "the Blue Building." This is where a water tank was -- was put at the time of the events. And this is the so-called White House, which became a detention site for men who were separated from their families before boarding buses. This large meadow is just in front, in fact, of the UN base. So this is another -- another view, coming from Bratunac town and going towards Potocari. This main building is the UN base. So this is the direction that the Serb soldiers coming from Bratunac took when they entered Potocari. After the UN base is another group of two factories. One is blue, and it's also called by the people "the Blue Factory," and that building was used by the Bosnian Serb forces during the days where they stayed in Potocari as their headquarters. Just in front of it is another building that was not occupied also during -- during these days. All the other factories were packed with refugees. So continuing the drive towards Srebrenica town, after the UN base the main facility is the Expres bus compound, which is a big compound with a big hangar, and that place was also crowded during these days. These buildings are those that are in front of factories that we saw previously. So this is the area of the 11 of March factory, houses in front. All these houses were also occupied by people during the days of the 12th and the 13th July. This -- it's not obvious on the film, but it shows a water pump behind a destroyed house. The reason why this water pump is filmed is because several witnesses relayed later on that they saw dead bodies near water pumps, but there are several of these water pumps in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And Mr. Ruez, the sites that you are pointing out to the Judges, the different factories, the different buildings, are those referred to by the witnesses in -- with regard to their statements about what occurred once they arrived in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. And this is the reason why we show all these pictures, so that once the witnesses will explain the situation that they have experienced during these days, the Court has an idea of how the -- how the locations look like. And this is the reason why I'm also using the names which are the names that the people who knew the place generally used, like 11 of March, zinc factory, Akumulator factory for the UN base.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Along those lines, Mr. Ruez, we have a series of photographs that show each of those particular buildings. Turning first to Prosecution Exhibit 2.2, you have an overview of the area with several buildings pointed out in particular, the first of which would be the UN headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The buildings of -- of importance on this picture are essentially the Akumulator factory, that is marked as being the UN HQ, headquarters. When one crosses the asphalt road, at the exit of UN HQ is a house that everyone refers to as "the White House." Many people talk about it, saying "the unfinished house." And this is the location where men that were separated from their families prior boarding buses were taken to.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Were you able to determine during the course of your investigation where the initial refugees sought shelter when they arrived in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The UN base was the first destination of -- of all the people who fled Srebrenica town. The UN Battalion there initially accepted the crowd and quickly the factory was overcrowded with about 5.000 refugees who took shelter in it. So once the facility was fully occupied, the UN Battalion stopped accepting refugees and the people found shelter in the vicinity of this main factory, so that is in all the factories nearby.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 2.3, there is another shot showing some of the factories in the area, the first of which would be the Expres compound.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. So this is a still view that indeed show it is Expres compound, and also at the right of the picture part of the so-called zinc factory. All these facilities were packed with people during the days of -- starting the 11 in the evening through the 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 2.4. There is the Energoinvest zinc factory. There are, Mr. Ruez, two factories that have the name Energoinvest; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. This one is the zinc factory. The other one is 11 of March factory. And on this one one can see also the type of landscape that is behind the factory. In this instance, there is a meadow and a house. These elements are important because some witnesses will come and give detail about things that they saw happening behind the factories.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 2.5, is the other Energoinvest factory that's commonly referred to as the 11th of March; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, correct. This is -- it corresponds to half-destroyed markings that were left on a picture of the building, that is written "Energoinvest," and "11 of March." This factory was also used by the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you indicated that Srebrenica fell on the 11th of July and the refugees fled to Potocari. On the day and evening of the 11th of July, was the Bosnian Serb army present in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No. The -- the 11 July -- the advance of the Bosnian Serb forces stopped in Srebrenica town. Potocari became the area where all these people assembled. There were sightings of Serb forces in the vicinity, some spotting of artillery positions on the hills around Potocari, but no physical presence of Serb forces and all the people we talked with report that that evening and that night was calm, the situation was very calm.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: During the course of your investigation, were you able to determine whether or not there was any contact on the 11th of July between the VRS, the Dutch Battalion soldiers stationed in Potocari, and any of the Muslim representatives of the refugee population?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: There was a first meeting on request of General Mladic. That meeting involved in the evening of the 11th. Colonel Karremans was the commander of the UN Battalion, and two of his assistants. And that meeting took place at the Hotel Fontana in Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I don't intend to go into the details of each of those particular meetings, as the Court will have the opportunity to see them on videotape. However, can you tell the Court, these meetings that were called, what was the purpose with regard to the refugees who were currently situated in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The main goal of these meetings, as it will be seen later, was for General Mladic to access representatives of the population. In fact, General Mladic wanted to -- to talk with military commanders of the BiH army from the 28th Division, and these people had already left the area, so no representative of the army could be found. And the civilian representatives had fled as well, so the only thing that the UN Battalion could do to fulfil the demand of Mladic was to try to pick educated people among the crowd and have them volunteer to have contacts with General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you bring up a good point, which is the presence of the 28th Division of the Bosnian army within the enclave. Prior to the fall of the enclave, when the population made a choice of either going to Potocari or trying to break out through the woods, was there a presence of the army within the enclave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. The -- the Bosniak armed forces in the enclave were known as the 28th Division, commanded by Naser Oric. The number of forces in fact was only dependent on the number of guns available. So the assessment that is done by the military observers, by the UN officers in the area, was that the 28th Division consisted approximately of 5.000 armed fighters.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: We'll discuss after the section on Potocari the events concerning the trek of the column. However, as you stated, it was General Mladic's intention to seek out and meet with representatives of the army at the Hotel Fontana; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: At the first Hotel Fontana meeting, were there any representatives, either military or civilian, present at that Hotel Fontana meeting?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No, there were no -- no representatives, neither of the army or from the civilian side. At the second meeting, one civilian representative showed up. His name is Nesib Mandzic. But as he will explain himself, he was not really a representative. He had no -- no role prior that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Was Nesib Mandzic selected as a Muslim representative by the Dutch?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, he was requested to -- to become a representative.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Did he in fact attend the second Hotel Fontana meeting along with the representatives of the Dutch Battalion?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: He was accompanied there by Colonel Karremans.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: The second Hotel Fontana meeting, when did that occur?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In the evening of the 11 July.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Was there a subsequent meeting held at the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Following the second meeting, General Mladic reiterated his demand to access military representatives, which again could not be found, since they were already trying to flee through the forest. So the next morning, the 12th July, arrived to discuss the situation with General Mladic three civilian representatives. Nesib Mandzic again, and also a woman Camila Omanovic, and another man, Ibro Nuhanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: At that third Hotel Fontana meeting, did General Mladic make any statements with regard to how the VRS or the Bosnian Serb army intended to deal with the refugee population?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. It is at this third meeting that for the first time General Mladic arose the issue of his intention to have all men aged from 16 through 60 years of age to be scanned in order to check if they were among well-known war criminals.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Did General Mladic indicate what would happen to the women and the children who were currently in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The emphasis during these meetings, when it was a question of deportation, the emphasis was put on the fact that free choice was given to the population, the choice either to leave or to stay. And if they wanted to leave, officially they could leave for the destination of their choice.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Based upon your investigation and your interviews, did the representatives at the meeting, Muslim or DutchBat, feel that General Mladic was sincere when he said that the population had the choice to stay or to go?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I don't know what the people who were present at this meeting were thinking about this. I have no idea. The only thing that we can observe through the investigation is that this alleged freedom of choice was very quickly cancelled by the behaviour on the ground of the Serb soldiers, once they entered Potocari. The obvious aim of that behaviour was to inflict maximum terror to the population and have them flee the area as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Was there an agreement between the Bosnian Serb army and the Dutch Battalion with regard to the escort of the women and children out of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The agreement was that UN vehicles could escort these convoys, that every convoy of refugees would be assisted with UN presence.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: How were the women and children going to be transported from the enclave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The operation that was set up was to attract in the area as many buses and trucks as possible and then to use these -- these vehicles in convoys and ship the population from Potocari towards Kladanj, that is, Muslim-held territory at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Roughly how far is it from Potocari to the confrontation line at Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: By the road, it is approximately 30 kilometres of distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: You indicated that the third Hotel Fontana meeting occurred on the morning of the 12th. When did the deportations begin?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: When the meeting was over, the third meeting dated 12 July, buses were already arriving in Potocari once the UN representatives came back to their headquarters, the buses were already there and very quickly the transportation started.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: You had indicated previously that throughout the day on the 11th and the evening of the 11th the Bosnian Serb army had not yet entered Potocari. By the time the deportations began, was the Bosnian Serb army present in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The Bosnian Serb army entered Potocari coming from the direction of Bratunac, at 12.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Based upon General Mladic's proclamation that all males between the ages of 16 and 60 would be separated, did the Bosnian Serb army set up a separation line in Potocari in order to effect that order?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. As soon as the deportation starts, the first measure that is taken is to set up a cordon of UN soldiers in order to conduct crowd control and avoid -- avoid the situation to become too chaotic. On this photograph that shows the area of Expres compound and zinc factory, at the left of the picture is a house and a path that leads to the asphalt road. More or less exactly at that location, at the end of this path, was set the line I am talking about. So the crowd was at the right of this photograph. There was then a first line of UN soldiers. The people went through this line. The buses were waiting for them at the left of this photograph. But behind the line of UN soldiers were also Bosnian Serb soldiers who started separating the men from the women and the children.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: For the sake of clarity, Mr. Ruez, you indicated that the UN actually set up their own cordon for crowd control; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. But in a measure to in fact protect the crowd from itself, to avoid that people would -- would rush towards these buses and harm themselves in that process.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Where did the Bosnian Serb army set up their separation checkpoint vis-a-vis the Dutch security cordon?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: They had soldiers just behind the Dutch -- Dutch line, and also soldiers along this asphalt road, and in between the buses. So as soon as this line was passed, the people were in immediate contact with the Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: When men were separated from their wives and their children, where were they taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: We have another photograph of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 2.2, there is an indication on the photograph which you've marked as "white house."

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The previous picture -- the left of the previous picture connects with the right part of this picture. So these two pictures could be a panorama if they were glued together.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And for the record, the previous picture was Prosecution Exhibit 2.3.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So at the right of the picture is again the asphalt road. So the men were taken -- taken along this road. They passed in between the blue building at the centre of the picture and the building named Blue Factory. And more or less, just before arriving at the UN HQ, at the left side of the road is the so-called white house or unfinished house, as some people call it, and this is the location where the men were taken at the moment after having been separated from their families and prevented to board buses.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: As discussed earlier, Mr. Ruez, there is a videotape which the Court will view concerning the events that occurred on these particular dates. Are -- have you had the opportunity to look at that video?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. We also have the Exhibit P2.6 that is a still picture of the white house.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: On the videotape which the Court will see later today, are you able to see the men -- the separated men in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The 12th July was present in the area a journalist, a Serb journalist, who could film in this -- in this place. And among the pictures he could film in this area was a short footage of this white house with men sitting on the balcony. The footage is interesting because it confirms also both the observations of a UN military observer who was on the spot and who could assess the house, where he could see that the house was crowded with men sitting on top each other, and also adds confirmation to the witnesses who reported having seen these men on the balcony, and the inside of the house was probably full of people, the reason why the men also had to sit on the balcony. Once the house was full, these men were then put onboard of buses, where they were not mixed with the other deported people. And from that white house they were then taken to Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: You have at this point, Mr. Ruez, the men being separated and taken to the white house and the women and children being put on buses to Kladanj. The route from Potocari to Kladanj, does that travel through Bratunac as well?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The direction to go to Kladanj is first going through Bratunac, then driving towards the so-called intersection of Konjevici or Konjevic Polje, then driving south towards Milici, then west towards Vlasenica, and then there is a last stop in a little location named Luke, and after that is a canyon which was the confrontation line at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Along that route, were there a series of checkpoints set up by the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, there were several checkpoints, more or less in all the main places that I just named. At these checkpoints the Dutch Battalion was escorting the convoys, were stopped, and their vehicles were taken from them, so they could not fulfil the mission that was initially agreed with General Mladic. They could not escort the convoys. At these checkpoints also more or less all the refugees that took the route report about harassment or threats that were -- that they received inside the buses, in addition to the robberies of their belongings and the fact that they had -- they were forced under threat to give valuables of whatever they had with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: You indicated that the Dutch vehicles were taken. What were the Dutch driving at that time?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: For the escort of the convoys, as far as I know, they were using four-wheel drive vehicles. The APCs that got captured by the Serb forces were captured prior to the deportation.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: In addition to their vehicles, did some of the Dutch soldiers have their personal UN gear taken as well?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. At these -- at these checkpoints, not only the vehicles were taken but also the equipment and their persons as well. They were taken in detention. One of the locations they were taken to was the compound of the 65th Protection Regiment in Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: In addition to not being allowed to fulfil their duty to escort the refugees to the end point in Luke, were some of the UN soldiers prevented from returning back to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. That also happened. But it also happened that some of them made the choice not to return to Potocari and to -- the decision to cross the line and reach Muslim-held territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: The UN vehicles and the UN gear, are they distinctively marked in terms of colour or insignia?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I don't know about that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Are you aware of whether or not the Dutch Battalion soldiers wore what is commonly referred to as blue helmets?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. That equipment was also taken from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Once arriving in Luke, were there a number or a few male individuals who had been able to board the buses and manage to pass each of the checkpoints along the way?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At the very beginning of the process, some men indeed could board buses in Potocari. And the filtering of -- of these men in Luke was quite weak at the beginning, and indeed some men had a chance to -- to make it up to Kladanj at the early stage of the operation, but that seems to have stopped quite quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Based upon your investigation, were you able to determine what happened to some of the men who managed to make it all the way to Luke?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Once arrived in Luke, they were separated from the women and then they were marched towards a little elementary school located a few hundred metres far from the spot where the buses were stopping, and they were kept in detention inside that elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: If we could turn back to Prosecution Exhibit 2.3. During the course of the day of the 12th, could you describe the security situation in Potocari. The Dutch Battalion, vis-a-vis the Bosnian Serb army, as well as the Bosnian Serb army, and the Muslim refugees.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At the beginning, the people felt reassured by the guarantees that were given by General Mladic, who addressed the crowd. But shortly afterwards, during the course of the day, the situation deteriorated. The Serb soldiers started mixing with the crowd. Some UN soldiers were stripped of their equipment. Refugees report seeing soldiers dressed like UN soldiers but speaking Serb, so they concluded that these were Serb soldiers wearing UN equipment. So people couldn't any more trust their environment, and the panic started to spread quickly, especially once separation started inside the crowd, when in the evening Serb soldiers started to separate men from their families among the crowd. And that same situation continued during the night, the separation process.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Was there a point in time when the convoys or the buses stopped for the night of the 12th?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I don't remember exactly at what hour, but at the end of the afternoon indeed the deportation process stopped, only to restart the next day, the 13th, around 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And you indicated that that evening, the night of the 12th, as the refugees waited for the buses to reappear again the next day, the atmosphere was one of panic?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: All the people we talked with referred to that night as a night of terror, terror for various reasons; the first one being indeed groups of Serb soldiers flashing their lamps in the dark to people and separate from the others whoever they wanted to pick in that crowd and leading people away, people hearing screams and not knowing what these screams were about. Their own imagination added to the terror. As an example, a person who was inside these factories and suddenly someone probably threw some -- some sand inside the building through a window, and everyone inside started panicking, wondering what poison was thrown at them. So there was a mixture of -- of terror, based on facts and also terror based on the anticipation and the fear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to object to this line of questioning. Number one, he is now offering a summary of witness statements that he has interviewed in the past and he is not offering a basis for the witness statements. We don't know who they are. And if they're being allowed to come testify for the Prosecution and we have an opportunity to cross-examine them, then his summary is valid under the new decisions. But if these are witness summaries from people that are not being called by the Prosecution, then the witness summaries that he's offering are hearsay upon hearsay, another level, which has been ruled in the Milosevic case to be inadmissible and unreliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think that the Prosecution has laid good foundations, asking some questions, and the witness also mentioned that during his talks with some witnesses who were present at that time. And whenever the Prosecutor asks a question, she will begin with the phrase like "during your interviews at that time and based on your investigations," such as things. We understand that the witness was not present at that time. All his testimony is kind of hearsay evidence. As I said before, that all those evidence, hearsay evidence, is admissible, we'll just bear in mind that point, and we understand later on through other witnesses there will be some corroboration evidence provided by the Prosecution. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just had one more object to mention. When she says "and the witnesses felt this," that calls for speculation. As long as it's documentary evidence of what occurred and he has evidence of that, we have no objection. But when it calls for him to speculate what they were feeling and the fear that they were feeling or the circumstances, then I believe it's outside the realm of his investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much to draw our attention to that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: When we elaborate this piece of the evidence, we will take into the consideration of your objection, to see how much weight or no weight at all we should attach to this piece of the evidence. Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Madam Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, based upon your interviews with the witnesses, were they able to describe both the events that occurred the evening of the 12th, how they perceived them, and how they felt based on those events?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand the point of the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: That's all right. Were you able to interview witnesses who described particular events that occurred the evening of the 12th?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I will not list the compilation of all the -- the crimes that the people did report during these interviews, since indeed some of them are going to come and will be direct witnesses here.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And I won't ask you to go into the details of each crime that you learned or was reported as having occurred that evening. However, did they convey to you, based upon what occurred the evening of the 12th, how they felt the morning of the 13th when they woke up?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think any one of them won't confirm one thing, and that is that in the morning of the 13th all the people who were in Potocari had only one desire, and this was to leave this place as soon as possible and board as soon as possible on a bus to get out of there.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And was their desire to leave the area immediately based upon the events that had occurred the night and the day before?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Definitely. On the 13th, in the morning, many women tried to find some -- sorry -- find some water in the area, and many statements talk about sighting of dead bodies near the water pumps or blood stains near water pumps, so it seems that there was an on-purpose intent to leave traces of murders committed nearby these water pumps in order to inflict maximum terror to the people who would discover that in the morning, all this and the clear intent to cancel this alleged freedom of choice that was given officially to the population.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this might be a good point to take a break, if the Court is agreeable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take a break for 30 minutes. We'll resume at 11.00? Yes, 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, before you proceed, Madam Prosecutor, I have to remind you about the time. I was told that this courtroom will be used by another trial, so we have to leave this courtroom at 1.45 sharp. We might have a break for 30 minutes during the two sittings, and you may control the pace to conduct your direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, before the break, we were discussing the various reports of incidents that occurred the evening of the 12th of July in Potocari. Were you able to take any one of those accounts and independently verify the information based upon your investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: The witness in particular whose information you were able to verify is an individual who will be and has been submitted by the Prosecution and whose testimony will be before this Court. However, can you explain to the Judges how after the fact you were able to go out to the scene and verify what you were told.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: If you turn to Exhibit 2.3.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No. The previous one was the good one.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Can you explain, using this picture, how it was that you were able to initiate the portion of your investigation that dealt with this particular witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. This witness reports a very specific series of incidents, that is, that he was hiding underneath a shed that is in fact located on the hill from which this photograph is taken but a bit underneath, and from there he could see the yard of the Zinc Factory, that is, at the right of the photograph, and he could see that some Serb soldiers were taking men away from this area and they were walking with them on this open area towards the arrow where it is written "fence." He then saw that these soldiers and their prisoners passed through a cut that was made in the fence. Then they walked toward the house that is at the bottom left of the picture, and in front of the house at the time of these events, that is, 12 July, there was a cornfield just in front of this house, which is not there on this photograph which is dated 1996, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 2.8.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I had not finished on the previous one. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: I apologise. We'll go back to 2.3.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. So the event that he describes happens at the angle of that -- that house, which is at the bottom left of the picture, and there he sees that these prisoners are banded on a kind of wooden log and one of the soldiers is hitting them, the men, with a kind of machete, at the back of his neck, and he was together with another man who did count, I think, approximately 80 -- 80 victims of this series of murders that happened behind this house. So once we -- we went on the spot to try to determine if there were some elements that could confirm the story. So indeed, when we go to the Exhibit P2.7, we could find that indeed one of these fences had a cut and on this picture there is a wooden stick that in fact keeps the cut open. The cut is large enough to enable men indeed to go through this fence. So then from there they walked towards where this truck is. The truck was not there at the time of the events. And then they walked left towards that house. The Exhibit 2.8 shows the approximate location of the execution site, and in front was supposed to be a cornfield with high corn. Once these people had been killed, a truck came and then the dead bodies were loaded on that truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, what is the significance -- you have the cornfield here marked. With regard to the witness's account, what is significant about that cornfield and its location?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: If this cornfield, at the time of the events, had been mowed or non-existing, this event would never have -- it would not have been possible for this event to happen here because approximately 30 metres away from this event was the crowd of people who were trying to get onboard the buses, so everyone would have seen the event. At the opposite, if indeed the corn of the field was grown, no one would be able to see from the road what was happening in that location, and most probably also no one would dare to get away from the main crowd and try to -- to move around in this area. So it was indeed a safe spot for killers to operate in that zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And were you able to verify whether or not the corn was indeed high at the time of the events in question?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. If we have a look at the Exhibit P2.9. So this photograph is an aerial imagery dated 13 July, so one day after the event that was reported by this witness. The various locations we're busy with at this moment are at the top of the picture. At the top right is written "shed." That's the location from where the witness could see the event. The other arrow at the left is marked "shed." It's another shed, but it's marked the location where in fact there was the cut in the fence. And what can be seen also here is that the cornfield in front of the house is indeed high. One can see the shadow of the corn at the bottom of this corn. And when one looks at the arrow marked "vehicle," there is a vehicle but it's pushed inside the corn, and one can see the shadow of the corn around this vehicle. So on this photograph, of 13 July, the corn indeed was high. What can be seen also on this picture and deserves being mentioned is the crowd of people which is inside the circle, and the location of UN APC is in fact the -- where the separation line is. But this photograph is the 13, and the 13, that line had moved towards north, that is, at the bottom of the picture. The day before, the separation line was more or less exactly at the exit of path that was leading to this killing spot. On the next exhibit, which is 2.10, so it's a blow-up of the same area but on a photograph dated 12 July. Unfortunately, the quality of the copy is poor, but nevertheless one can see a difference with the previous one. First, the separation line indeed is located in front of that house and the path that leads to the killing site. And the vehicle that was pushed inside the cornfield the 13 was in fact on the path the 12, so one could ask himself why this vehicle was moved between the 12th and the 13th to be pushed into the cornfield. This seems to match what the witness declares when he says that a truck came to load with bodies and take them away. In order for that bus -- for that truck to come to the spot, indeed this vehicle was blocking the way and was then pushed in the cornfield.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: When you conducted this portion of your investigation in an attempt to corroborate this witness's account, did you in fact go to each of the places that are depicted on these photographs and view them from the ground?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: The point from which the witness indicates that he observed these events take place, were you in fact able to verify that you could see that particular area from that location?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. I did not overload the presentation with photographs, but indeed we have additional photographs that show the precise location from where these men could see the events, and being at that location indeed one could see at least the area where he indicates the events happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you indicated earlier in your testimony that as the refugees fled Srebrenica there were two courses of action, one being the flight to Potocari and the other being the trek of the column. Leaving Potocari, you have the separated men detained in the White House. You indicated that separated men have been detained near the confrontation line in Luke and the women and children are in Kladanj. With regard to the men who chose the latter option, that is, to attempt a breakout of the enclave via the woods, can you explain using Prosecution Exhibit 2.11 the route that that column intended to take?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Where did the column first assemble in an attempt to begin their trek out of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: On the 11th, in the afternoon, all the men who did not make the choice to go to Potocari assembled at the north-west of the enclave in the area of the villages Jaglici and Susnjari. From there approximately the figure that the people mentioned when they are asked how many people were there approximately, the -- more or less all come up with a figure of approximately 15.000 -- I mean, 15.000 -- sorry, 15.000 people. Among this crowd, this crowd can be in fact split in two groups. One is the army and the other one is men without weapons. As I indicated previously, the number of soldiers of the 28th Division was determined by the number of weapons available. So approximately one-third of that large group carried a weapon. The armed men were put in front of this -- this column and there was an additional group of armed men at the end of the column and in between there were also people who were carrying rifles, hunting rifles, and things like this. So the process that started during the night, once night fell, there was a path opened in the mine field at the limit of the enclave and the people infiltrated the area one by one going through this mine field. That led to a column stretched on several kilometres, and the evacuation of this area lasted the entire night of the 11th to the 12th and also the morning of the 12th. The last ones getting out of the area of Susnjari left before noon the 12th July.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Taking a look at Prosecution Exhibit 2.11, in the course of their trek towards the Bosnian free territory, was there a point as which they had to cross an asphalt road in order to continue the journey?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. But what happened during this -- this trek is that most of the people did not know the area. Most of the people who were inside the enclave were coming from the area of Zvornik, of Vlasenica, places around but they didn't know specifically this -- this terrain. So the instruction that was given to the people was to follow a power line that is running on a hill just south of the road that goes from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje. So this trek is marked in green. The intention was to cross the asphalt road close to Konjevic Polje, follow the valley of Cerska, turn around Udrc Mountain, and then hit north direction Nezuk and try to break the lines in the area of Nezuk. That scenario didn't function like it was initially planned. The column suffered a lot of attacks through shelling but also infiltration of Serb soldiers, so quickly the column was broken in various pieces. Ambushes occurred. And by the end of the day of 12 July the large group of the army who was in front of the column broke through the lines at the level of the intersection of Konjevic Polje. But once this first large group managed to pass these lines the area was sealed off by the Drina Corps and all the area which is marked on this map with a red line shows in fact the blocking position that was set in order to block this -- this column. All those who could not manage the cross the 12 in the afternoon were trapped behind that line and were wandering in this area in small groups, sometimes in huge groups, still continuing to suffer attacks, did not know exactly where to go and what to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I wish to object to the narrative form to the response from Mr. Ruez. He was not answering any question. He had entered into a narrative, and I would like to ask the Court to ask that we keep this question-answer form on direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Well, Ms. De la Torre, I think you have to ask questions to lead the witness to the points where we need.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 3.2, Mr. Ruez, you have indicated on this photograph a power line. Is this the power line you were referring to earlier as the point of reference for those attempting to escape the enclave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The aim of this exhibit is to enable the Chamber to have an idea of how the terrain looks like in this area. This area is the area of the village of Kravica. The hill at the right of the photograph is the hill behind which this column was progressing, and this power line is indeed the reference point for them to know in what direction they had to go to.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Moving on to Prosecution Exhibit 3.3. This photograph depicts an intersection. Can you explain to the Court the significance of this particular intersection.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a photograph of the intersection of Konjevic Polje when coming from the direction of Zvornik, so looking towards south, and the big hill that is just in the middle of this picture is the last hill on which the column arrived before trying to cross the asphalt road. So this is an area -- in between this spot and the previous one, this is the entire area where the people who could not cross this asphalt road the 12 in the afternoon were trapped behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Going back to Prosecution Exhibit 3.2 and taking into account the terrain that you saw both in the last picture, 3.3, as well as this one, were the individuals who were trapped behind the line, given the terrain, able to see the Serb positions along the road?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, they did. And this is what they were doing the 13th in the morning. Overlooking this asphalt road, they could see Serb forces all along but they could also see UN vehicles, UN APCs, they were hearing calls, calls to surrender, calls that were giving them safe guarantees. What they didn't know for sure at that moment is that some of the blue helmets that they could see on the road in fact were worn by Serb soldiers, as we will see later on in one footage, and that the UN APCs driving around were in fact vehicles that had been stolen from the UN Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Based upon your interviews of individuals who survived this particular ordeal, were they able to describe to you the situation they found themselves in on the 13th, given the fact that they were now trapped behind this road and that the Serbs had taken up positions all along the line?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The 13th in the morning, after having suffered many attacks during the night, the people who later on survived the detention process indeed explained that that morning a massive surrender process started, since some groups followed the instructions that were given to them from the Serb soldiers who were on the asphalt road and started a surrender process. And once they started, other groups followed. So in the morning of the 13th a massive surrender process started in this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Given the terrain at that particular -- at this particular point, Mr. Ruez, were there natural collection points or funnel points for individuals who decided on the morning of the 13th to go ahead and surrender to the Bosnian Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. There were two main funnel points, one is for those who were the most east in this area between Konjevic Polje and Kravica. These ones went down a valley that was leading them to a meadow named Sandici. In reality, there were other meadows also used in this area and where the prisoners were assembled, but ultimately all those who were on various fields in this area of Kravica-Sandici were taken to Sandici and were made to sit on a large meadow. More at the west, those were on -- in the area of a big hill above the intersection of Konjevic Polje. These ones surrendered in that area on the asphalt road and most of them were led towards the little town of Nova Kasaba, where they were kept on a football pitch.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 3.4, you'd indicated that one of the main collection points was at Sandici. There is an aerial photograph dated July 13th, 1995. Can you describe for the Court what this particular photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. So one can see in the middle of the picture the asphalt road that goes to the right towards Konjevic Polje, to the left towards Kravica and Bratunac.
